newsitem.title: USA: John Hancock exits health care, focuses on core.
newsitem.headline: John Hancock exits health care, focuses on core.

text.p: John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co will turn its attention to its core retail life and investment management businesses after agreeing on Friday to sell its health insurance business to WellPoint Health Networks Inc for $86.7 million.
With the transaction, John Hancock exits the health insurance business but will retain its group long-term care business and other unrelated stand-alone group life business.
John Hancock chief executive Stephen Brown, in a telephone interview with Reuters, said he was optimistic about the outlook for the company's group long-term care business.
"We think long-term care insurance has a terrific future," Brown said.
Hancock, the nation's ninth largest life insurers, also is among the market leaders in group long-term care, he said.
The company has about a 25 percent market share in group long-term care insurance and is one of the top five sellers of retail long-term care insurance, Brown said.
He said he sees opportunity for additional growth by marketing the company's products to employees in the workplace.

Proceeds from the deal, which is expected to close no later than January 31, 1997, will be invested in Hancock's core businesses and will be used to expand the distribution of its retail products, Brown said.

"We have a very detailed strategy of expanding the distribution of our retail products. In investment and pension we have a number of initiatives that will require additional capital in order to expand," he said.
Brown said the company decided to sell its small heatlh insurance business after deciding that it would need a substantial capital investment in order to compete.

"As we reviewed all of our businesses and looked to the future in terms of what kinds of capital investments each business would require in order to grow it and be successful, we felt that we really had to make choices and decide where to put our resources in the future," he said.

"We felt a lot of capital would have had to have been invested in the group health business to be competitive and we felt this was not the best use of our capital and somebody who specializes in the health business, such as WellPoint, would be better able to utilize our health business," he said.
Brown said John Hancock was in talks with other companies in addition to WellPoint, but he declined to identify them.
A.M. Best senior vice president Larry Mayewski said John Hancock's health insurance business made only very minor contributions to the company's overall bottomline.
"It was very negligible to say the least," Mayewski said.
The group health and related life businesses that Hancock has agreed to sell to WellPoint currently provides services to an estimated 1.4 million medical members.
The acquisition also includes Hancock's estimated 1.3 million dental members.

The move to sell comes as companies like John Hancock look to streamline their operations and redeploy capital into more profitable businesses as they deal with increasing competition in the financial services industry, he said.
